gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Apple specs the current MacBook Air (M5) for 'up to two external displays over a single Thunderbolt port', while the M2 Air drives one external display and the M3 Air drives one with the lid open. So on a Mac, a single-cable MST USB-C KVM (AV Access KD-E10) mirrors the two monitors, as AV Access says itself, and you only get two extended screens from a Thunderbolt-path KVM (TESmart HDC202-X24) or a two-cable KVM (AV Access iDock M10) on M3-in-clamshell, M4, M5 or Pro/Max Macs. No KVM gets a base M1 or M2 past one screen.
standout_why: Racksandwatts (cited) says only 'On macOS, the MST route gives duplicated external screens' for the iDock C10 and never names an Apple chip. The TESmart buying guide (cited) never mentions MST and says only 'Some Apple Silicon MacBooks support only one external display without using DisplayLink-based solutions'. The Office Journal laptop+desktop guide (rank 2) mentions none of DP Alt Mode, MST, Thunderbolt or MacBook display limits. None of them says that Thunderbolt carries two streams where USB-C MST cannot, and none gives Apple's per-chip counts. Rivals already cover part of it: mirroring through MST.
decides: This splits the pick by laptop. On a Windows laptop with USB-C DP Alt Mode, the cheaper single-cable MST KD-E10 ($169.99) extends to two screens. A MacBook M4/M5 or Pro/Max owner needs the Thunderbolt HDC202-X24 (one cable) or the iDock M10 (two ports, $289.99). An M3 Air owner gets two screens only with the lid closed. An M1 or M2 Air owner gets one extended screen whichever KVM they buy, so they should buy a 1-monitor KVM or a DisplayLink dock. This confirms our page's 'Mac: two extended screens' column and gives it Apple's own wording.

findings.label: External displays over one cable
findings.value: Up to 2 external displays (6K60 or 4K144 each) over a single Thunderbolt port, with the built-in display active
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'Supports up to two external displays over a single Thunderbolt port' and 'Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports support native DisplayPort 1.4 speeds (up to HBR3) with DSC capability'. This is the Thunderbolt path that lets a one-cable Thunderbolt KVM extend two screens.

findings.label: External display limit
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'. No dual-monitor KVM can extend two screens on this machine.

findings.label: External display limit
findings.value: 1 external display with the lid open; 2nd external (up to 5K60) only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M3, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display with up to 5K resolution at 60Hz'.

findings.label: Mac behaviour with two monitors
findings.value: Mirrored (MST not supported by macOS); extended on Windows laptops
findings.note: Maker's wording: 'MacOS doesn't support USB-C MST (multi-stream transport), so two duplicate contents will be displayed.' Laptop port spec: 'USB C supports: 100W Charging (DP 2.0), USB 3.0 (up to 5Gbps), and up to 4K@60Hz (DP MST) two video transmission'.

findings.label: Laptop charging source
findings.value: Up to 100 W, passed through from the laptop's own adapter
findings.note: Maker's wording: 'When charging your laptop, please additionally use your laptop's original adapter.' The included adapter powers the switch only.

findings.label: How it gets two extended screens on a Mac, and which Macs
findings.value: Two USB-C/Thunderbolt ports on the Mac (dual-head cable); M4/M5 and Pro/Max: 2 extended; M3 base: 2 only in clamshell; M1/M2 base and Intel Macs: 1
findings.note: The maker says two USB-C/Thunderbolt ports are required for dual extended displays. Its comparison table lists the M10 as 'Extended' where most models are 'Mirrored'. Page states: 'This model is not compatible with a MacBook + Windows laptop setup.' 100 W PD.

findings.label: Why Thunderbolt and not MST for a Mac
findings.value: Needs a supported Thunderbolt 4 laptop; macOS does not use MST for two extended desktops; up to 60 W charging on the PC1 path
findings.source_title: How to Share Two Monitors Between a Thunderbolt Laptop and a Desktop PC | TESmart (2026-07-28)

Designed for 'one laptop with a supported Thunderbolt 4 connection'. Higher-power laptops 'may charge slowly or still need their original adapter'.
